reading: Washington University in St. Louis operates the Genome Data Center, a computing facility supporting the McDonnell Genome Institute, formerly known as the Genome Sequencing Center, at the university's School of Medicine in St. Louis, Missouri. The university's own facilities management department publishes a dedicated page for the Genome Data Center, confirming it as real, currently documented infrastructure. The McDonnell Genome Institute is one of the best known genomics research centers in the United States, having played a major role in the Human Genome Project and continuing to conduct large scale DNA sequencing for cancer research, infectious disease, and other genomics focused work, all of which requires substantial data storage and computing capacity to process sequencing output. This is a research computing facility serving the university's genomics programs rather than a general purpose enterprise or commercial data center, and no specific critical IT megawattage figure was found published for it during this research, consistent with how academic research computing facilities are typically described in terms of storage and processing capacity rather than commercial colocation metrics.

sources.title: Genome Data Center, Operations and Facilities Management, Washington University in St. Louis
